messages:
sam: Heads-up — p99 in the Latency dashboard for /v2/generate is showing ~220ms but the endpoint breakdown for that same route shows p99 ~= 480ms for a subset of hosts. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

maya: I noticed that earlier this morning on a canary rollout. Which aggregation window are you looking at?

sam: 1m rollup, last 2 hours. The global line chart (top) is 220ms but when I click into endpoint split, one backend host spikes the p99 to ~480ms. Global should reflect that, right?

igor: Not necessarily — we do traffic-weighted rollups. If the host with 480ms only handles 2% of traffic, the weighted p99 can still be ~220ms. The console label doesn't make that distinction very explicit.

jess: Ah okay. We're currently showing a single p99 badge and it's ambiguous whether it's weighted or unweighted. UX ask: label it or show both p99_weighted / p99_per_endpoint.

analytics-bot: rollup job "latency-tdigest-rollup" finished at 1732109600. config: {method: tdigest, compression: 200, window: 60s}.

maya: tdigest compression can under-estimate extreme tails in some distributions. If that host's samples are heavy-tailed and low-volume, tdigest may compress away the spike.

igor: Yep. Two levers: 1) compute weighted percentiles at rollup time (gives a network-level p99), 2) keep per-endpoint raw percentiles (unweighted). We currently only expose the first one in the main card, which is misleading.

sam: Could we show both and add a tooltip explaining "weighted by request count"? Quick fix then improvements later?

jess: +1 for both. Also add a per-endpoint histogram mini-chart in the breakdown flyout. Low-effort: reuse existing histogram component and cap rendering to top 10 endpoints.

igor: Implementation notes: our rollup job emits tdigest serialized blobs per route. To get per-endpoint true percentile, we need to either keep raw sample reservoirs per endpoint (expensive) or recompute from raw logs on demand. I can prototype a hybrid: store reservoir of 10k samples per endpoint for last 1h, use that for percentile UI.

maya: Another angle — the console's sampling for the host split uses srv sampling at 1/10 when traffic > 50req/s which will bias per-endpoint percentiles if not properly reweighted. I think we have two bugs: sampling mismatch + ambiguous rollup meaning.

sam: Can someone run a quick experiment to recompute p99 from raw samples for that host and confirm 480ms is actually real (not a noise spike)?

analytics-bot: running query: 
```
SELECT approx_percentile(0.99, latency_ms) as p99, count(*) as n
FROM requests
WHERE route = '/v2/generate' AND host = 'be-17' AND ts > now()-interval '2 hours'
GROUP BY 1;
```

analytics-bot: result -> p99=482ms, n=1,842.

sam: so it's real. Not a 1-sample fluke.

jess: Next steps:
- UX: Change label to "p99 (traffic-weighted)" on main card and add a small "compare per-endpoint" toggle. (owner: jess)
- Infra: Add reservoir sampling per-endpoint (10k) for 1h to support accurate per-endpoint percentiles on UI (owner: igor)
- Telemetry: Emit metadata on rollups that indicates method (tdigest/compression) + sample_count so we can show a fidelity warning (owner: maya)
- Audit: backfill last 24h for /v2/generate to compute divergence metric and create alert if |weighted_p99 - max_endpoint_p99| / max_endpoint_p99 > 0.25 (owner: sam)

sam: I'll open a ticket with the audit query and link this thread.

igor: Quick note on accuracy tradeoffs — tdigest is great for space, but for tails we should set compression >= 400 for high-traffic routes or fall back to reservoir when endpoint volume < threshold.

maya: Also consider exposing in the rollout UX whether canary traffic is being downsampled — that was the case earlier and made the canary tail invisible in route-level metrics.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/endpoint-reservoir @igorss (PR #4521) — estimated CI 12m.

jess: Nice. For the console copy I can add a small "Why do these differ?" inline helper that mentions weighting, sampling, and tdigest compression.

sam: Thanks all. Once igor has a short prototype we can test on a staging route and verify the p99 alignment. :thumbsup:

maya: One more: add a small smoke test in eng-infra that compares raw p99 vs rollup p99 on deploy to catch regressions.

igor: will do. pushing an RFC for reservoir sizes and compression thresholds by EOD.

sam: Great. Marking this resolved for now, follow-up in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
